title: Accidents Involving Food and Goods Delivery Platform Workers and Compensation and Support Provided
what_it_is: Accidents Involving Food and Goods Delivery Platform Workers and Compensation and Support Provided

sections.label: Fatal delivery worker accidents
sections.summary: Since January 2021 there have been five fatal work-related traffic accidents involving food and goods delivery platform workers, while the Advisory Committee on Platform Workers examines financial protection for work injury.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Since January 2021, there have been five fatal work-related traffic accidents involving food and goods delivery platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In parallel, the Advisory Committee on Platform Workers is looking at strengthening financial protection in case of work injury for delivery persons, private hire car drivers and taxi drivers.

sections.label: Mandatory work injury reporting
sections.summary: Implementing a work injury financial protection framework would require mandatory reporting of work injuries so platform workers receive necessary compensation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The implementation of such a work injury financial protection framework would require the mandatory reporting of work injuries to ensure platform workers receive the necessary compensation.

sections.label: WICA coverage for gig workers
sections.summary: The question asks the Senior Minister of State to confirm whether WICA's policy intent covers persons on flexible working arrangements and why gig economy flexible workers are not covered.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: First, can the Senior Minister of State confirm that the Work Injury Compensation Act (WICA) policy intent is to cover persons on flexible working arrangements and, if so, why not cover flexible workers in the gig economy?

sections.label: Self-employed gig worker coverage
sections.summary: Gig workers are self-employed and not covered under the Employment Act, but the Advisory Committee is examining whether WICA can apply to gig workers subject to platform algorithm management controls.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The underlying reason is because gig workers, by definition, are self-employed persons and self-employed persons are not covered under the Employment Act.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Having said that, the Advisory Committee, having consulted widely, is looking at this issue from the perspective that self-employed workers in the gig economy may be subject to management controls by the algorithms in the platforms, in which case, they are somewhat a little bit more employee-like.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: And, therefore, we are looking closely to see whether WICA can be applied also to gig workers, to provide them a lot more financial protection when they are injured in terms of their work.

sections.label: Company employee benefits
sections.summary: The company would then be expected to provide employee benefits to this worker under the Employment Act.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The company would then be expected to provide employee benefits to this worker under the Employment Act.

sections.label: Advisory Committee report timing
sections.summary: When the Advisory Committee was announced last September to look at gig workers' savings and the injury framework, the Senior Minister of State also announced its report would be ready in the second half of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: When the Senior Minister of State announced the formation of the Advisory Committee last September to look at savings of gig workers and the injury framework, the Senior Minister of State, I believe, also announced that the report of the committee would be ready in the second half of this year.
